local_articles.snippet: 4) and 800m freestyle (Sept 25). At the last Games, Singapore bagged just one swimming medal through Teong Tzen Wei’s men’s 50m butterfly silver. Earlier in the swim meet, China’s 13-year-old prodigy Yu Zidi set a Games record when she won the women’s 200m butterfly final in 2:05.08, ahead of teammate Chang Mohan (2:08.44) and Japan’s Misa Okuzono (2:09.67). The teenager shaved almost half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei’s mark of 2:05.57 set in 2023. The home crowd had much to cheer about in a thrilling men’s 200m individual medley final when Japan’s lone Paris 2024 swimming medallist Tomoyuki Matsushita pipped teammate Yumeki Kojima by 0.06sec to win in 1:55.30. China’s defending champion Wang Shun was third in 1:57.14. Singapore’s Reagen Cheng set a personal best of 2:01.25 in the morning heats, shaving almost a second off his previous best of 2:02.11, and finished 10th in 2:02.65

questions.title: Who will be the first person charged in the United Kingdom over alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide?
questions.background: British authorities have been investigating allegations involving Rwandan genocide suspects living in the United Kingdom.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official public charging announcement from the United Kingdom’s Crown Prosecution Service. Resolution : Identify the first individual formally charged in the United Kingdom in connection with alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, provided the charges are announced by December 31, 2026. Arrests without charges, extradition proceedings, and charges brought outside the United Kingdom do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The person’s full name as given in the charging announcement.
questions.current_reasoning: Scotland Yard's War Crimes Team has investigated six Rwandan genocide suspects in the UK since 2018 and confirmed in December 2025 that two investigations are at an advanced stage with full files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (one submitted in late 2023, a second by late 2025), while none had been charged as of May 2026. The two CPS files almost certainly come from the four named suspects interviewed voluntarily in 2020—Celestin Mutabaruka (Kent), Celestin Ugirashebuja (Essex), Emmanuel Nteziryayo (Manchester), and Dr. Vincent Bajinya, who legally changed his name to Vincent Brown (London)—whereas fifth suspect Charles Munyaneza (Bedford) suffered a stroke and was only interviewed in 2024, and a sixth suspect arrested in Gateshead in January 2024 remains publicly unnamed. Splitting Bajinya's ~20% share between his UK legal name 'Vincent Brown' (11%) and birth name 'Vincent Bajinya' (9%) reflects CPS charging announcement naming conventions while leaving 19% for Munyaneza and unnamed suspects.

questions.title: Which former minister from Viktor Orban's government, if any, will have parliamentary immunity lifted in September 2026 to permit an embezzlement investigation?
questions.background: The party that won Hungary's 2026 parliamentary election campaigned on tackling corruption. Parliamentary immunity can prevent prosecutors from pursuing criminal investigations against legislators unless Parliament lifts it.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Hungarian parliamentary records or contemporaneous reporting from reliable news organizations identifying former ministers whose immunity is lifted. Qualifying Event : Hungary's Parliament must vote during September 2026 to remove a former Orban-government minister's immunity specifically to allow prosecutors to pursue an embezzlement investigation. Allegations alone, without the parliamentary vote, do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the former minister's full name. If no former minister qualifies during September 2026, resolve as no qualifying minister.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-18 calendar-decay update: Two more full business days (Sept 17-18) elapsed since Sept 16 with ZERO international wire reports (Reuters/Straits Times/Al Jazeera/Irish Times) of any Chief Prosecutor (Legfobb Ugyeszseg) immunity-waiver petition to Parliament, despite Reuters's Budapest bureau actively covering two Hungarian anti-corruption stories on Sept 15 (Volanbusz raids/Daniel Jellinek and former FM Peter Szijjarto's private-jet complaint—note Szijjarto resigned his parliamentary seat July 15 and holds no immunity). With only 12 calendar days left in September and the Friday close arriving before Monday Sept 21-22's plenary window, time decay nudges 'no qualifying minister' up 0.48 -> 0.51 and trims Balazs Hanko 0.39 -> 0.36 (keeping the shift modest because Hungarian-language Exa queries returned empty results on Sept 17-18, warranting caution against Hungarian-index lag). questions.title: Which Indian cricketer will publicly say by September 20, 2026, that the 2027 men's ODI World Cup will be his last for India?
questions.background: The men's ODI World Cup is the global championship for cricket's 50-over international format.
